rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas-evidence/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill. It has `---` front matter with a `name`, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions`.

The requirement has one MUST for each site: the description must state when to use the skill in terms of the user's task. The `description` in the front matter does this.
- It opens with "Use when Habeas evidence needs creating or refreshing".
- It goes on to name the situations that trigger the skill: `habeas coverage` or `habeas status` reporting missing, stale or false evidence, uncovered `{test}` lines, FIXME judgments, citation or site reviews, or disagreeing assessments.
- It covers a user who phrases the problem loosely, with the example "the habeas test is failing".
- It also says what the skill covers, which is running `habeas author` and fixing what it flags.

The description also says "If evidence went stale because code or requirements moved, use habeas-refactor first." The requirement's MAY allows naming another bundled skill where an agent could confuse the two, so this is permitted. It also helps separate the two skills. I did not open the `habeas-refactor` skill to confirm it exists.

The requirement lists no violation queries. I found no gap.
